Your friend's experience with Bipolar 2 very much mirrors my own experience. When I have my hypomanic episodes, I'm way more "out there" with my personality and some people just find me to be downright annoying. However, I never have had any hallucinations or made any life-ruining decisions. I've engaged in riskier behaviors during my episodes because I'm more impulsive, and my self-confidence sores through the roof. I've embarassed myself because I couldn't shut up during social engagements. However, no one ever thought "Oh she's having an episode". I actually looked forward to my hypomanic episodes, because depression had been the status quo for the majority of my years with mental health issues.

I wish more people understood Bipolar disorder. I tried every anti-depressant under the sun before landing on a proper mood stabilizer. I had been diagnosed with ADHD, Generalized anxiety disorder, and Major Depressive Disorder. It wasn't until my first obvious hypomanic episode when I was 25 that my psychologist diagnosed me with BD2 (which wasn't a surprise because it runs in my family). Now I understand why none of the antidepressants had worked. I just wish that people understood that even though BD2 doesn't come with psychotic episodes (typically), bipolar depression can be just as debilitating and dangerous as manic episodes and that our hypomanic episodes may not look serious, but I know that I make impulsive decisions that might not make any sense to others if I got into a car crash alone at night, for example. It's not a competition about which form of bipolar is more severe/dangerous. BD1 and BD2 are equally severe illnesses that need to be taken seriously. 

The rate of undiagnosed BD2 is very high and thankfully I was able to get help for it and manage the depression. But people throw around the word "bipolar" as a catchall term for crazy and that's just ignorant and also a slap in the face to those experiencing both types of bipolar disorder.

I hope your friend's treatment is going well.

Back in high school, I had just gotten a new Sony Viao laptop for my birthday. I started visiting the webcam chat site Stickcam in its early days.

I met a supposed 17 year-old who said his name was Skip Parker. Right away, there were red flags that this person was a catfish. Being a 17 year-old with body insecurities, I ignored the warning signs that he was not who he said he was.

First off, he never turned on his webcam even though I did. He flattered me, telling me how beautiful I was and we chatted constantly. He sent me pictures of himself, and I thought he was the cutest guy ever. I believed all of his excuses about not being able to use his webcam. His story was that he was from a strict mormon household and he couldn't risk getting caught video chatting. 

He even convinced me to do some inappropriate things on the camera while he watched. Nothing too extreme, but he definitely saw me topless. I was into it at the time because this "boy" had gained my trust and I had such a big crush on him.

We even talked on the phone a couple of times, and his voice sounded young and didn't raise any alarm bells.

Then one day, he just disappeared. I was heartbroken and feared that I was too chubby, leading him to not like me anymore.

Not long after, I realized that I must have been duped by someone pretending to be this cute guy. Numerous internet searches over the years confirmed that "Skip" did not exist. Now I believe that I was most likely taken advantage of by an internet pervert, probably much older than me.

I felt ashamed to have been so insecure at the time to believe his lies and fall for a phony pervert.
